To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the majority of the older adults are not aware of cancer prevention, and the majority of them do not engage in cancer‐preventive behaviors.

1) the elderly population is a growing segment of our society, 2) the elderly population will continue to grow in size and proportion to younger age groups, 3) there are few cancer prevention programs targeted toward the elderly, 4) there is little evidence that cancer‐specific primary interventions are being used with the elderly, and 5) there is a lack of research in this area.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the prevention of cancer and the promotion of healthy ageing.
the development and application of new technologies to the study of the human genome, with the ultimate goal of understanding the genetic basis of human health and disease.
the development of a new approach to cancer prevention in older adults.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
primary prevention of cancer for the elderly is a promising and potentially beneficial strategy, but the evidence is limited.
the current state of knowledge on primary prevention of cancer in older adults is not adequate.
there are no conclusive statements regarding the efficacy of any of these approaches to primary prevention.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we need to understand more about the health behaviors of the older population, and that we need to develop more effective ways to disseminate research findings to the older population.
we have shown that there are a number of opportunities to promote healthy lifestyle choices in the geriatric population.
primary prevention is not only a priority for the elderly, but it may be a necessity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to do more research on the effectiveness of interventions to promote cancer‐specific primary preventions in the elderly.
there is a need to develop and test interventions for older adults that address their specific needs and preferences for health behaviors and health promotion.
there are a number of barriers that need to be overcome in order to promote primary prevention of cancer in the older population.
